question.text: Who currently approves the cleaned Marsh reel for the listening booth, and which package names connect that handoff?

messages.content: For the wetland exhibit, the cleaned Marsh reel is the audio package we call Tern. The unedited takes stay on the field recorder until the exhibit closes.
That separates the listening copy from the raw recordings.
I keep the recorder in the equipment cupboard. The exhibit captions use the species names approved by the local bird group.
The foyer display uses the Reed slideshow, and Niko approves its captions. Visitors can borrow the large-print captions at the ticket desk.
I can distinguish the foyer display from the listening booth.
The foyer projector is on a timer that stops at six. The ticket desk also holds the tactile map of the trail.
When Tern reaches the listening-booth team, they file that same audio package as Evening set. The delivery folder keeps the original Tern label as well.
The two labels describe the same delivered audio package.
I send booth deliveries to the shared exhibit folder. Elias checks that each audio file opens before it goes into the booth schedule.
The outdoor walk uses the Dawn set, and Elias signs off its playback. It is separate from the listening-booth schedule.
The outdoor playback has its own approval scope.
The walking group starts at the north gate. Rain moves the talk into the potting shed, but the start point stays the north gate.
The caption review happens on Tuesdays with Niko. The listening booth uses over-ear headphones because the foyer gets noisy.
Those arrangements cover captions and visitor playback.
Spare headphone cushions live in the booth drawer. The volunteer rota is posted beside the exhibit door each Friday.
Priya is now the approver for Evening set in the listening booth. Elias still checks file playback, but that check is not the approval.
Priya approves the booth package; Elias checks whether its files play.
Priya wants approval requests in the exhibit folder. The booth is closed on Monday mornings for cleaning.

question.text: As of May 20, where should Mara collect glaze sample boxes for weekday studio pickups, and when did that arrangement take effect?

messages.content: Mara collects glaze sample boxes for weekday studio pickups from the North gallery locker. The locker is beside the loading entrance.
The weekday glaze pickup point is clear.
We put invoices in a separate tray at reception. Mara uses the studio van for the boxes and cycles in for paperwork.
I suggested the South foyer for weekday glaze pickups while the gallery floor is repaired. Mara has not agreed to that suggestion.
The South foyer is still a proposal.
The repair crew stores cones in the South foyer. The Saturday pottery class continues to collect its samples at the kiln door.
The studio van needs a height clearance of two metres. The West annex entrance has enough clearance for it.
That entrance is suitable for the van.
Mara prefers pickup slips printed on plain paper. We keep packing blankets on a rack inside the annex.
Mara and I agreed that weekday studio pickups of glaze sample boxes move to the West annex, shelf C, starting May 12. The North gallery locker stops serving those pickups then.
The agreed location and effective date replace the old weekday pickup point.
Reception still handles invoice collection. Saturday class samples still go out through the kiln door.
I found an April 8 pickup note while sorting the files: Mara used the North gallery locker for glaze boxes that day. The note belongs with the April records.
That note describes an earlier pickup.
The April sample inventory was printed in green ink. The gallery locker key stays with the exhibition attendant.
Mara used shelf C in the West annex for this morning’s weekday glaze pickup. The new pickup slips identify that shelf by letter.
This morning’s pickup follows the agreed move.
Invoice slips still say reception. The Saturday class list still says kiln door, so I keep those slips in separate folders.

question.text: What is the recorded venue decision for the summer sound workshops, what reason supported it, and does that reason still hold after the staffing update?

messages.content: I chose to keep the summer sound workshops at Dock Hall because its evening technician is included in our hire. Avoiding a separate technician fee is the reason for that choice.
The venue choice rests on the included evening technician.
The summer sessions start after six. I keep the daytime school demonstrations on a separate booking sheet.
Dock Hall lends us twelve folding chairs with each hire. We bring our own microphones for the sound workshops.
That covers chairs and microphones for the booking.
The school demonstrations use the library room. Those demonstrations finish before the library closes at four.
A friend suggested moving the sound workshops to Birch Studio. I have not adopted that suggestion; its shorter walk from the station is appealing, though.
Birch Studio is an option you are considering.
Birch Studio’s courtyard suits the daytime picnic. I booked that courtyard for the volunteer lunch, which is separate from the workshops.
Dock Hall says that from June 1 its evening technician will be charged separately. The summer sound workshops run in July, so the included-technician arrangement will not cover them.
The stated fee change affects the reason given for the summer venue choice.
Daytime Dock Hall hires still include a room attendant. Our school demonstrations remain daytime library bookings.
The transport grant can cover workshop participants’ bus tickets. It cannot pay venue staffing charges under the grant terms.
The grant covers participant travel but not venue staffing.
I store the grant receipts by workshop date. Volunteers can claim bus tickets through the same receipts folder.
Dock Hall remains my recorded choice for the summer sound workshops; I have not changed the venue booking since the staffing notice. I will review the extra cost before deciding whether to move.
The current recorded choice remains Dock Hall pending your review.
I have not booked Birch Studio for the sound workshops. The volunteer lunch booking in its courtyard remains in place.

question.text: 河岸口述歷史的訪談裡，受訪者想暫停錄音時，要怎麼示意？暫停後由誰決定何時繼續？

messages.content: 河岸口述歷史的訪談安排在週三下午，地點是社區閱覽室。每次訪談由一位主持人和一位收音志工一起進行。
時間、地點和人員分工都清楚了。
受訪者可以帶一位親友陪同。親友的交通補助和受訪者一樣，採實報實銷。
我們為訪談訂了一個小動作：受訪者只要把掌心朝向主持人舉起，就表示先別把談話收進音檔。主持人看到後會請收音志工停機。
這個手勢可以讓受訪者不用出聲就先停下錄音。
沒有舉手時也可以直接口頭提出休息。手勢和口頭要求都由主持人接應。
河岸展覽的開幕式採用紙本流程表，主持人拿藍色那份。舞台音控看到主持人指向手錶時，會播放下一段音樂。
開幕式有自己的舞台提示方式。
開幕式的攝影只在舞台區進行。訪談室不會直播到舞台螢幕。
河岸口述歷史的訪談停機休息後，是否重新開機要等受訪者說可以。主持人不能因為下一位在等，就自行恢復收音。
是否繼續由受訪者決定，排程不會代替這個確認。
休息時志工會把錄音設備留在桌上。訪談前的設備測試使用志工自己的聲音。
訪談錄音整理後先送逐字稿給受訪者確認。沒有取得受訪者同意的段落，不會放進河岸展覽的聆聽區。
逐字稿確認和展覽使用都有受訪者的同意流程。
聆聽區提供耳機，字幕另外放在桌邊。展覽導覽員不參加訪談錄音整理。
我把訪談邀請函改成大字版，方便長輩閱讀。邀請函仍請大家提早十分鐘到閱覽室。
大字版保留原來的報到安排。
陪同親友可以坐在受訪者身旁。茶水放在門邊，和錄音設備分開。

question.text: Who borrowed the Alder projector at 16:10 on May 9, and which room did that borrower take it to?

messages.content: The Alder projector belongs to the media desk and has a padded grey case. The Birch projector belongs to the teaching cupboard and has a black case.
The cases distinguish the two projectors.
The media desk keeps lens cloths in a drawer. Teaching staff collect cupboard keys from reception.
Nora hosts the sketch group in Studio D on Mondays. Her group uses the wall whiteboard rather than a projector.
The sketch group has its own room and equipment arrangement.
Nora takes group attendance on paper. She stores the sketch materials in the tall studio cabinet.
The media desk log has an Alder projector loan at 16:10 today. The borrower-name field on that entry is blank.
The log records the loan time without a borrower’s name.
Alder loans are due back the next morning. The padded case has to come back with the projector.
That 16:10 Alder loan entry records Studio D as the room the borrower took it to. The room field and the blank name field are on the same entry.
The room is recorded even though the borrower is unidentified.
The desk closes at five on Saturdays. Returns left after closing go on the indoor cart by reception.
Owen returned the Birch projector after the Sunday photography class. His class meets in Studio B and uses the black projector case.
That return concerns Birch and the photography class.
The class lights stay dim during slide review. Owen leaves the class sign-in sheet with reception.
Leena prepares the media desk’s weekly equipment report. Preparing the report does not mean she borrowed every item listed in it.
The report author and equipment borrowers have different roles.
Leena labels damaged cables with a paper tag. Intact spare cables go in the low equipment drawer.

question.text: Has the weekend book club adopted Lantern Cafe as its June meeting venue?

messages.content: The weekend book club met at Lantern Cafe for a one-off March reading. That trial booking covered only the March meeting.
The March cafe booking has a limited scope.
The club reads one novel each month. Members bring their own copies rather than borrowing a club set.
The weekend book club agreed to meet in the Ash courtyard for April and May. That venue agreement does not set the June location.
The agreed courtyard dates stop after May.
The club keeps its shared notes in a paper binder. The binder stays with whoever hosts that month.
I suggested Lantern Cafe as the weekend book club’s June venue. The club has not accepted that suggestion; we are waiting for members’ travel dates.
The June cafe suggestion is awaiting a club decision.
The cafe can seat eight people indoors. The weekend book club currently has seven regular members.
The Wednesday cycling group has adopted Lantern Cafe as its June meeting venue. Its rides begin from the cafe entrance.
That adoption concerns the Wednesday cycling group.
The cycling group meets before its ride each week. Its route sheets are kept in the cafe’s blue folder.
The weekday reading circle booked Lantern Cafe for its June lunchtime discussion. The reading circle has a different membership list from the weekend book club.
The lunchtime booking belongs to the weekday circle.
The weekday circle discusses essays instead of novels. Its organiser sends a reading link two days before each lunch.
I checked the weekend book club’s venue notes today: June still contains the Lantern Cafe suggestion, with no accepted venue entered. Members are still comparing their June travel dates.
The weekend club notes still show a suggestion rather than an accepted June venue.
The May meeting remains in the Ash courtyard. I will circulate the next novel’s title before we settle the June location.
